1. Lucky-draw mechanism, which the loop underweights. The tip's seeds 0–2 sit about 0.2 pp above its population mean. So any idea that keeps the RNG consumption identical (same step count and the same randint/randperm calls) inherits that luck on seeds 0–2. Any idea that changes step count or sample order regresses toward about 0.7526 before its own effect is counted. This predicts that RNG-preserving tweaks look like −0.1 to +0.1 on seeds 0–2, while RNG-changing ones look about 0.2 pp worse than their true effect. It explains E020, E021, E024 and E029 as near-misses at about 0.752–0.753. Feasibility from here on is mostly decided by whether the RNG stream is preserved.
2. Time model. The run is GPU-bound and costs about 23 ms per step on average, roughly 27 ms at 32 px versus about 19 ms at 20 px. Converting a 24 px step to 20 px saves about 5 ms (E026). Backward work near the stem is memory-bound and expensive. In E028, truncating group 1 and the whitening path in the tail saved 0.84 s (13%) for −0.2 pp, which is the best time-per-pp trade seen so far. The whitening bias still has requires_grad=True after step 75, so its input-gradient and GELU backward work at full resolution is wasted. Setting requires_grad=False after step 75, in a second captured graph, is an untested bit-identical saving of about 2–4%.
3. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026). Late low resolution, or a big jump into the 32 px tail, costs 0.3–0.9 pp (E011, E018, E024). I don't believe the stem-whitening mismatch matters much, because GELU, BN and Muon adapt quickly.
4. Plateau. Weight decay, label smoothing, Muon lr and the averaging ramp all land within ±0.2 pp (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025). Muon has no wd, so the wd change acted only on the SGD groups. The LR schedule is not flat in the other direction: halving the warm-up cost 0.21 pp at identical RNG (E029). The warm-up protects the BN-bias/whitening-bias SGD groups, whose lr is 64×. A longer warm-up may help, or at least be neutral.
5. Noise. The 3-seed SD after an RNG re-draw is about 0.25 pp. A rebuild moves the mean by about 0.05 pp. With an identical RNG stream, the 3-seed delta noise is maybe 0.1–0.15 pp.
6. Epoch dial. Each −0.25 epoch saves about 0.14 s and costs about 0.12 pp.

W5 (contrarian), after E029. Tip E027: 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of steps, 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0–2. Its held-out mean is only about 0.7526.
1. Lucky-draw mechanism, which the loop underweights. The tip's seeds 0–2 sit about 0.2 pp above its population mean. So any idea that keeps the RNG consumption identical (same step count and the same randint/randperm calls) inherits that luck on seeds 0–2. Any idea that changes step count or sample order regresses toward about 0.7526 before its own effect is counted. This predicts that RNG-preserving tweaks look like −0.1 to +0.1 on seeds 0–2, while RNG-changing ones look about 0.2 pp worse than their true effect. It explains E020, E021, E024 and E029 as near-misses at about 0.752–0.753. Feasibility from here on is mostly decided by whether the RNG stream is preserved.
2. Time model. The run is GPU-bound and costs about 23 ms per step on average, roughly 27 ms at 32 px versus about 19 ms at 20 px. Converting a 24 px step to 20 px saves about 5 ms (E026). Backward work near the stem is memory-bound and expensive. In E028, truncating group 1 and the whitening path in the tail saved 0.84 s (13%) for −0.2 pp, which is the best time-per-pp trade seen so far. The whitening bias still has requires_grad=True after step 75, so its input-gradient and GELU backward work at full resolution is wasted. Setting requires_grad=False after step 75, in a second captured graph, is an untested bit-identical saving of about 2–4%.
3. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026). Late low resolution, or a big jump into the 32 px tail, costs 0.3–0.9 pp (E011, E018, E024). I don't believe the stem-whitening mismatch matters much, because GELU, BN and Muon adapt quickly.
4. Plateau. Weight decay, label smoothing, Muon lr and the averaging ramp all land within ±0.2 pp (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025). Muon has no wd, so the wd change acted only on the SGD groups. The LR schedule is not flat in the other direction: halving the warm-up cost 0.21 pp at identical RNG (E029). The warm-up protects the BN-bias/whitening-bias SGD groups, whose lr is 64×. A longer warm-up may help, or at least be neutral.
5. Noise. The 3-seed SD after an RNG re-draw is about 0.25 pp. A rebuild moves the mean by about 0.05 pp. With an identical RNG stream, the 3-seed delta noise is maybe 0.1–0.15 pp.
6. Epoch dial. Each −0.25 epoch saves about 0.14 s and costs about 0.12 pp.
Unsure: how results transfer to the PCIe judge, where 40 seeds at a population mean of about 0.7526 is above 0.75 but thin; the true cost of the wasted whitening backward; whether a longer warm-up buys accuracy.

forecasts.reason: About 9% fewer steps saves about 0.4 s, but loss-based pruning on short CIFAR-100 runs costs about as much as the epoch dial. The RNG re-draw also loses the tip's luck on seeds 0–2, so it likely misses 0.753.
Averaging knobs are flat (E025, E009). With the RNG stream preserved, the score stays near the tip's lucky 0.7547, and the held-out gain will be under 0.15 pp.
LS sits on a plateau (E013). An abrupt loss switch late in training perturbs BN-bias SGD at 64× lr; expect about −0.1 to 0 pp.
33 steps move from 24 px to 20 px for about −0.16 s (2.7%). The RNG is preserved, so seeds 0–2 stay correlated with the tip, but the hypothesis's 2.5% and 0.15 pp thresholds sit right at the edge.
GELU, BN and the trainable group 1 absorb stem statistics. Extra eigh calls add about 20 ms, and the gain will be under 0.15 pp.

cruxes: Is the tip's seeds 0–2 score a lucky RNG draw, about +0.2 pp over a held-out mean of about 0.7526? If so, only RNG-preserving changes can stay feasible on seeds 0–2. Test: run any null reshuffle, such as a different but equivalent randperm call order, on seeds 0–2.

How much time is spent on the whitening and group-1 conv1 input gradient after the whitening bias is frozen at step 75? Setting requires_grad=False is bit-identical, and a gentler FreezeOut variant could keep E028's 4 s/pp trade at a smaller accuracy cost.
Does a longer LR warm-up, the direction opposite to E029, raise accuracy at identical RNG and time? That would fund another epoch-dial cut.
